doc.title: Mona Hinton interviewed by Milt Fillius and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Neighbors in St. Albans: Basie and other musicians
summary: Hintons lived near Basie and many famous musicians and athletes.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That’s right. And one of the things that we’re doing in this series, initially, is we’re trying to develop some history of the Basie band. Now two things occur to me. First, the area in which you live is the same area that Basie lived in.
We lived right around the corner from each other before they moved down to Freeport.
And don’t a number of musicians live in that area?

Oh, at one time we had oodles of — well Illinois Jacquet and Wild Bill Davis still live near there. But we had Lena Horne lived there, and Ella Fitzgerald and oh gosh, who else? What’s his name, James Brown moved there later, Cootie Williams, I can’t remember, there was Jackie Robinson and Roy Campanella lived right down the street from us. I know I’m going to miss somebody.
Did you ever have a jam session in the middle of the street?
No because everyone was going his different way. It’s probably seldom that they were ever home at the same time.
